intervention.description: Evaluation of molten salt corrosion behavior

structure.description: Dual-phase microstructure with body-centered cubic phase (B2)

evidence_units.mechanism: Selective dissolution of the body-centered cubic phase attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe. The work function increased with increasing temperature, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation and protected the underlying BCC-B2 phase with enrichment of noble elements in the protective surface layer.
evidence_spans: Here, the molten salt corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt at 450 °C and 650 °C in comparison to conventional duplex stainless steel 2205 (DS2205).
The EHEA showed a significantly lower corrosion rate of ~1 mm/year at 450 °C compared to ~8 mm/year for DS2205.
There was selective dissolution of the body-centered cubic phase in both the alloys, B2 in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and α-Ferrite in DS2205.
This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.

evidence_spans: Similarly, EHEA showed a lower corrosion rate of ~9 mm/year at 650 °C compared to ~20 mm/year for DS2205.
There was selective dissolution of the body-centered cubic phase in both the alloys, B2 in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and α-Ferrite in DS2205.
This was attributed to micro-galvanic coupling between the two phases in each alloy that was measured in terms of Volta potential difference using a scanning kelvin probe.

Additionally, the work function increased with increasing temperature for AlCoCrFeNi 2.1, indicating that the FCC-L1 2 phase acted as a barrier against further oxidation and protected the underlying BCC-B2 phase with enrichment of noble elements in the protective surface layer.

intervention.description: compared corrosion resistance against 304 stainless steel

evidence_units.mechanism: superior pitting corrosion resistance attributed to the dual-phase structure and unconventional alloying approach
evidence_spans: This EHEA exhibited an excellent combination of high yield strength (~750 MPa) and ductility (elongation ~18%) at room temperature [ [22] , [28] ]. However, the molten salt corrosion behavior of dual phase HEAs for potential use in CSP systems has not been reported so far, and fundamental understanding of the underlying high-temperature corrosion mechanisms is lacking.

intervention.description: calculation of Gibbs free energy of formation for chloride corrosion products

structure.description: Predicted reactivity order of alloying elements with molten salt

evidence_units.mechanism: Thermodynamically driven selective depletion based on Gibbs free energy of formation (ΔG°), where elements with lower ΔG° for chloride formation are more likely to react and leach out
evidence_spans: Based on ΔG° for formation of chloride corrosion products shown in Figure 7 (calculations at 450 °C and 650 °C), the alloying elements present in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 are expected to show high reactivity with the molten salt in the following order: Al > Cr > Fe > Co > Ni.

material.name: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1
material.initial_state: lamellar arrangement of FCC (L1_2) and BCC (B2) solid solution phases

intervention.description: Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP) measurement of work function

structure.description: FCC (L1_2) phase shows higher work function than BCC (B2) phase

evidence_units.mechanism: Micro-galvanic cell formation where the phase with higher work function (FCC L1_2) acts as cathode and the phase with lower work function (BCC B2) acts as anode
evidence_spans: The potential contrast difference between the phases in AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 was approximately ~50 mV, while in the case of DS2205 it was ~35 mV, which explains the selective dissolution seen from the EDS maps, due to the micro-galvanic cell formation in both the alloys.
